newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1997 deficit seen at 3.5 pct - Paris COE.
newsitem.headline: French 1997 deficit seen at 3.5 pct - Paris COE.

text.p: Sluggish growth in 1997 is expected to leave the French 1997 budget deficit at 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, above the Maastrict treaty criteria for monetary union, the COE economic forecasting unit of the Paris Chamber of Commerce and Industry said on Wednesday.

The private forecasting body said it expected French gross domestic product to be 2.1 percent next year, below the government's forecast of 2.3 percent, partly because planned cutbacks in public spending would be restrictive in the short term.
COE economist Christian de Boissieu said, however, that even if the budget deficit were above three percent, France would still be allowed to join monetary union in 1999.
"France will be at 3.5 percent (of GDP) but I think it will pass its entry test," he said. "The markets have already discounted the possibility of some slippage as long as it is not too big."

The COE forecasts take into account the 37.5 billion franc payment from France Telecom, and other transfers. Without these offsetting factors it said the budget deficit would be 4.1 percent in 1997 and 4.3 percent in 1996.
